findings.title: Preserve texture axes deliberately projected out of neighborhood fetches
findings.scenario: A valid Neighbors3D<f32> Stencil with Texture2d R32Float input extent 4×4 and Texture3d R32Float output extent 4×4×2, no size/index parameters, e.g. a center-returning source. Both texture resources fit normal device limits.
trace: program.rs emits output Texture3d workgroups and the output bounds guard; coordinates.rs emits vec3<i32>(global_id.xyz).

grid.rs:83-86 uses vec3<i32>(textureDimensions(input).xy, 1) for this input; fetch.rs:30-35 deliberately uses coordinate.xy for every Texture2d 3D sample. The former frozen source has the same grid, coords, and projection at stencil.rs:489-493,542-546,614-646.

The earlier program therefore repeats the input plane along output z: z never participates in an input address. The new declared_axes yields [4,4,1,1], and cover_output takes three axes solely from neighborhood dimension. It returns OutputCoverage{Z,required:2,available:1} before dispatch.
This is a new behavior restriction on an explicit retained cross-kind fetch path, not an unsupported request for a new dimension or arbitrary shader capability.
findings.minimum_connected_repair: Carry the actual input fetch projection into output-axis coverage. Admit only axes that reach the input texture address, while retaining all actual coordinate conversion and neighbor/boundary arithmetic admission before projection. Do not weaken Buffer flattening/capacity or fourth-dimensional flat-prefix checks.
acceptance: The 4×4 Texture2d -> 4×4×2 Texture3d Neighbors3D path remains admitted and preserves plane repetition under Clamp and Wrap.

Axes participating in emitted i32(global_id), coordinate+1/-1 and modulo/clamp operations remain representable even when a later fetch discards them; allowing projected-away z must not silently admit signed overflow.
Retain restrictions on actual sampled x/y axes, checked population/divisors, input reflected stride/capacity, Buffer output prefix, empty-output ordering and actual device dispatch limits.
Keep native numerical/load/projection tokens and existing fixture population; no new tests/cases/helpers/assertions requested or authored.
Complete the connected pre-repair thirteen-lens inventory before implementation and repeat all relevant source reviews on the repaired frozen successor.

contracts.family: Stencil declared axes versus emitted grid
contracts.evidence: Host and native declarations agree on all explicit size shapes, input texture extents, output-derived axes and DEFAULT_NEIGHBORHOOD_SIDE=64. One-dimensional Buffer size vectors and fourth-dimensional plane size are typed rejected because native expressions do not support those shapes. The discovered defect is coverage of a deliberately projected-away texture axis, not a wrong grid declaration.

contracts.family: Stencil Buffer coordinates and physical capacity
contracts.evidence: Buffer outputs unflatten _global_index for 2D/3D regardless of input kind; Four uses the same flat-prefix path for all outputs. Host output population stays within declared grid. Buffer input capacity derives from logical byte extent divided by actual reflected native stride; maximum signed flattened index is population-1, with widened checked product and explicit u32 divisor bound. Logical bytes remain the later native binding prefix; incomplete trailing bytes do not become another record.

Positive axes avoid zero modulo/division. Clamp bounds extent to i32::MAX so last+1 is representable. Wrap checks 2*extent-1, covering (coordinate%extent+extent) before final remainder for admitted coordinates. Buffer grid population-1 bounds nonnegative signed flattening intermediates. Four/three flat divisor products are checked before native conversion. See GSL-C1 acceptance for projected-away output coordinates.
